title: Google Analytics internal template doesn't interact with cookie consent
body:
In the current implementation of the Google Analytics internal template, there seems to be no way to disable analytics based on user preference through a "cookie consent" interface. These are increasingly common, and it would be nice if there were a way for the internal template to honour a runtime request not to set cookies.

At the moment the template allows for the honouring of a browser Do Not Track preference, and the entire code is wrapped in a `doNotTrack` boolean. That completely prevents the use of analytics for users who set this browser preference, which is fantastic. However, so far as I can tell there's no way to influence the value of this variable from outside the template. And there's (understandably) no way for javascript to toggle the browser DNT preference.
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
I believe you can turn on `useSessionStorage` to [disable the use of cookies](https://gohugo.io/about/hugo-and-gdpr/#googleanalytics). But I haven't tested this myself and I'm not sure if this is even GDPR compliant.

You should note that Google Analytics v4 doesn't support disabling cookies at all. #8264 

As for consent. What about using localStorage. You would need to set `doNotTrack` to true before GA loads then remove it after consent.
```js
if (!doNotTrack && !localStorage.getItem("doNotTrack")) {
...
}
```

comments.author: Participant 1
Participant 2
Participant 1
comments.body:
Oh, that's a clever side effect of the choice of variable name, and something I'd not cottoned onto. I guess it also relies on the fact that the `var doNotTrack = (dnt == "1" || dnt == "yes");` assignment doesn't change the existing value of doNotTrack if dnt is undefined.

So maybe the substance of this issue should be to document that since it's non-obvious to people who only occasionally dabble in javascript (I asked several people before opening the issue :)).

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: I agree that it should be documented. I'll see what I can come up with later this week.
